⛳ TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP ROUND 1 RECAP — MIN WOO LEE LEADS AT -8 AT EAST LAKE ⛳

The 2026 Tour Championship is underway at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, and after Round 1, it's an unfamiliar name at the top of the leaderboard — and a very familiar one lurking three shots back.

ROUND 1 LEADERBOARD:
🥇 Min Woo Lee — -8 (solo leader)
T2: Viktor Hovland, Collin Morikawa, Chris Gotterup — -6
T5: Scottie Scheffler — -5 (birdie-birdie finish)
T8: Ryan Fox, Adam Scott, Gary Woodland, Tommy Fleetwood, Sam Burns, Matt Fitzpatrick — -4
T20: Rory McIlroy — -2

Min Woo Lee set the pace in commanding fashion, posting an 8-under round to take a three-shot lead. His playing partner, J.J. Spaun, had to withdraw during the round due to a shoulder injury, leaving Lee to play solo late in his round — but it didn't slow him down at all.

Scottie Scheffler — the No. 1 seed for the fifth consecutive year — carded a 5-under and closed with back-to-back birdies to stay firmly in contention. He is three shots back and has four rounds left.

Rory McIlroy had a rocky start, going 2-over early before rallying all the way to -2. At T20, he has ground to make up — but McIlroy has charged at East Lake before.

Round 2 is today. $40M purse. $10M to the winner. The FedExCup is on the line.

Who wins the 2026 Tour Championship? 👇

🏆 FIVE CONSECUTIVE NO. 1 SEEDS — SCHEFFLER IS REDEFINING THE STANDARD OF EXCELLENCE IN GOLF 🏆

When Scottie Scheffler arrived at East Lake Golf Club for the 2026 Tour Championship, he carried with him a distinction no player in PGA Tour history has ever owned: five consecutive years as the No. 1 seed in the FedExCup Playoffs.

Not three. Not four. FIVE. In a row.

Scheffler has already locked up his $23M FedEx Cup bonus. He has 21 PGA Tour wins to his name. He won the FedExCup title in 2024, and now he is attempting to claim his second — and to write another chapter in what is becoming one of the most dominant stretches in modern professional golf.

After Round 1, Scheffler sits at -5, three shots behind leader Min Woo Lee. It is a manageable deficit heading into a four-round tournament, especially for a player who closed the opening round with back-to-back birdies — the kind of finish that speaks to the mental and physical ability to accelerate when others are comfortable.

East Lake is where careers are defined. Scheffler has built the résumé. Now he is after the crown.

Do you think Scheffler wins the FedExCup again? 👇

facebook.long_form:
🎯 RORY MCILROY IS CHASING HISTORY AT EAST LAKE — BUT HE OPENED WITH A SHAKY START 🎯

Rory McIlroy has won the FedExCup three times — in 2016, 2019, and 2022. No player in history has ever won it four times. This week at East Lake, McIlroy has the chance to stand alone as the most decorated FedExCup champion of all time.

But after Round 1? He has work to do.

McIlroy opened the Tour Championship at 2-over par before rallying all the way back to finish the round at 2-under. He sits in a tie for 20th place — six shots behind leader Min Woo Lee and three shots behind the nearest contender he considers a direct rival in the chase for history.

The good news: East Lake is one of golf's best venues for comebacks. The format rewards consistent play over four days. McIlroy has won here before, and he knows how to close at this level.

The challenge: Scheffler is at -5, playing with characteristic efficiency. And Lee at -8 is playing with the confidence of a man who has nothing to lose.

Three rounds remain. The record is still within reach. But McIlroy needs to move — fast.

What does McIlroy need to shoot in Round 2 to get back in this? 👇

facebook.long_form:
💔 LIV GOLF'S FUTURE HANGS IN THE BALANCE — AND THE SPORT'S FOUNDERS ARE SPEAKING IN FUNERAL TONES 💔

The 2026 LIV Golf season is over. The final event concluded in Indianapolis, with La Sasso winning the individual title and Rahm claiming his third consecutive LIV individual championship. Legion XIII won the team title. And then the lights went dim.

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund — the financial engine that made LIV possible — has announced it is withdrawing its backing at the end of the 2026 season. LIV CEO Scott O'Neil has spent the last several months searching for a new investor, telling reporters that a signed deal is in place and that he hopes the transaction closes in September. If it does, LIV Golf 2.0 would continue — though with fewer events and reduced prize money.

But the men who made LIV are not sounding optimistic.

Greg Norman, the league's founding commissioner, said in a candid interview: "I hate to see it wither away. I would rather just see it end."

Ian Poulter, one of LIV's most visible ambassadors, posted on social media: "I genuinely haven't decided yet" whether to stay with the tour, adding: "I think time might run out."

More than 50 professional golfers' careers and livelihoods remain in limbo pending the outcome of O'Neil's investor negotiations.

Do you think LIV Golf survives into 2027? 👇
